problem:
$$
v=[\begin{aligned}a \\ b \\ c\end{aligned}],\,A=[\begin{aligned}21 & -13 & -9 \\ 20 & -12 & -9 \\ 18 & -12 & -7\end{aligned}]
$$

The vector $v$ and the matrix $A$ are given above. 
If $v$ is an eigenvector of $A$ that corresponds to the eigenvalue $\lambda =1,$ then what is the value of $\frac{a}{c}?$

activity_context.topic_title: Calculating the Eigenvectors of a 3x3 Matrix With Distinct Eigenvalues

feedback.problem:
$$
v=[\begin{aligned}a \\ b \\ c\end{aligned}],\,A=[\begin{aligned}1 & 4 & 0 \\ 0 & -2 & 3 \\ 0 & 0 & 7\end{aligned}]
$$

The vector $v$ and the matrix $A$ are given above. 
If $v$ is an eigenvector of $A$ that corresponds to the eigenvalue $\lambda =7,$ then what is the value of $\frac{b}{c}?$
feedback.worked_solution:
To compute the eigenvectors of a matrix, we need to find non-zero solutions of the matrix equation 

$$
(A-\lambda I)\text{x}=0.
$$

 

In our case, we have $\lambda =7.$ So, we get 

$$
\begin{aligned}A-\lambda I & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 4 & 0 \\ 0 & -2 & 3 \\ 0 & 0 & 7\end{aligned}]-7[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-6 & 4 & 0 \\ 0 & -9 & 3 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

To find the eigenvectors, we have to solve the corresponding homogeneous system of linear equations:

$$
{\begin{aligned}-6{x}_{1}+4{x}_{2}=0 \\ -9{x}_{2}+3{x}_{3}=0 \\ 0=0\end{aligned}
$$

Notice that its augmented matrix $M$ is already in row echelon form:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}-6 & 4 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & -9 & 3 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

In the reduced matrix above, there are two pivot columns (the $1$st and the $2$nd). Thus, ${x}_{3}$ is a free variable. From the second equation, we obtain ${x}_{2}=\frac{1}{3}{x}_{3}.$ Substituting this into the first equation, we get 

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} & =\frac{2}{3}{x}_{2} \\  & =\frac{2}{3}(\frac{1}{3}{x}_{3}) \\  & =\frac{2}{9}{x}_{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the general solution is

$$
[\begin{aligned}\frac{2}{9}{x}_{3} \\ \frac{1}{3}{x}_{3} \\ {x}_{3}\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{3}\in R.
$$

Setting, for instance, ${x}_{3}=9,$ we get the following eigenvector:

$$
v=[\begin{aligned}a \\ b \\ c\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 3 \\ 9\end{aligned}]
$$

Finally, $\frac{b}{c}=\frac{3}{9}=\frac{1}{3}.$
